📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bellingham finished 11th in the 2026 Ballon d'Or.

Is there a better central midfielder on the planet than Jude Bellingham right now?

Not according to Jose Mourinho. The Real Madrid manager might be trying to manage the Englishman's minutes, but he did not hold back in his praise after the 23-year-old came off the bench and scored a superb volley, helping Real overturn a half-time deficit to beat PSV Eindhoven 5-1.

"He has physicality, he has technique, he has tactical understanding of the game, he has ambition, he has absolutely everything," Mourinho remarked.

"He's an absolutely extraordinary player and for me, without any doubt, the best midfielder in the world.".

Bellingham's impressive 45-minute cameo came just nine days after an outstanding, all-action display for England in a 3-2 Nations League win in Spain.

'Extravagant, brilliant!' - Bellingham's wonder goal.

While the former Birmingham and Borussia Dortmund player also earned plenty of plaudits for his displays at the 2026 World Cup, where he scored seven times, Mourinho believes Bellingham's unique blend of craft and graft isn't yet fully appreciated.

"He can play as a '10', as an '8', with two pivots, with one," Mourinho mentioned after the win against PSV. "That's why I said, when the Ballon d'Or was discussed, that it was outrageous he wasn't among the top 10.".

While wingers like Lamine Yamal or Michael Olise are also likely to be contenders for the 2027 award, is there anyone you would rather have in central midfield than Bellingham?

BBC Sport looks at what makes him so good, and who his closest challengers are.

Is Bellingham currently 'the best player in the world'?

Although only 23, Bellingham is already in his fourth year at Real Madrid and is on course for his most productive campaign since his debut season in 2023-24, when he scored 23 goals and provided 13 assists, including setting up Vinicius Jr in the Champions League final.

He has seven goals and four assists in 18 appearances this season. Only three central midfielders have more goal involvements across Europe's top five leagues, but Bellingham's all-round game is what sets him apart.

He leads his Real team-mates for possession won, duels won and fouls won. And while only Kylian Mbappe has had more shots on target, Bellingham offers far more than just late runs into the box.

He has played more passes into the final third than any other Real player, leads the club for ball carries and is second only to Arda Guler for chances created.

When Bellingham's coaches at Birmingham gave him the number 22 shirt, it reflected their belief that he could play any role, as a number 10, 8 or 4.

He has fulfilled that potential to become the complete midfielder.

While Bellingham made his senior debut with Birmingham, Vitinha also spent part of his formative years in the Midlands, scoring once in 22 appearances during a loan spell at Wolves - a spectacular long-range strike against Chorley in 2021.

But goalscoring isn't what the Portuguese playmaker is best known for - it is his metronomic passing.

The 26-year-old has played a pivotal role in Paris St-Germain's back-to-back Champions League triumphs, with manager Luis Enrique saying he "embodies the perfect midfielder".

He was named man of the match in the victory over Arsenal last season, having completed 141 of his 150 passes, matching the Champions League final record set by Barcelona's Xavi in 2011.

Vitinha finished third in the Ballon d'Or voting in 2025 but slipped to 14th this year, a ranking Luis Enrique disagreed with.

According to recent reports, "It's a real pleasure to have a player with such physical abilities and that mentality," the PSG boss remarked last month. "He's at an incredible level.".

Rice finished one place below Vitinha, and four below England team-mate Bellingham, in the 2026 Ballon d'Or rankings after helping Arsenal win their first Premier League title since 2004.

Recent findings suggest that he briefly played at centre-back as a youngster at West Ham before establishing himself as a top-class defensive midfielder for the Hammers. But since joining the Gunners in 2023 he has taken his game to another level, adding significantly more attacking output.

Rice created 17 substantial chances in the Premier League last season, as defined by Opta, a total bettered only by Bruno Fernandes and Rayan Cherki.

Saving Nepal’s wild orchids — in photos

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, prized for their ornamental and medicinal value, hundreds of orchids are illegally harvested and sold each year.
  • Sources indicate that A couple of hours drive from Kathmandu, in the hills near Chitlang village in central Nepal, a group of locals and forest officials gather in a dense subtropical woodland.
  • Bashyal refers to this team as a taskforce — one on the hunt for illegal activity.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, prized for their ornamental and medicinal value, hundreds of orchids are illegally harvested and sold each year. Now, conservationist Reshu Bashyal is leading an effort to protect them.

Words by Saugat Bolakhe and photos by CJ Karki.

Sources indicate that A couple of hours drive from Kathmandu, in the hills near Chitlang village in central Nepal, a group of locals and forest officials gather in a dense subtropical woodland. Beneath a canopy of pines, Himalayan chestnuts and Nepalese alders, the group listens as wildlife conservationist Reshu Bashyal guides them through a questionnaire designed to document the signs of poaching.

Bashyal refers to this team as a taskforce — one on the hunt for illegal activity. But instead of focusing on animals, as many conservation projects do, the group’s objective is to protect flora, specifically orchids. These flowering plants are harvested and sold across Nepal’s borders.

The flowers are prized for their ornamental value, but they are also used in traditional medicines, including Chinese, Tibetan and Ayurveda healing products.

In a recent development, multiple parts of the plant, including the stem and fruit, can also be used as ingredients. “It’s as if these plants have some magical properties about them,” Bashyal states.

Nepal has more than 500 orchid species, many of which are heavily harvested. Between 2008 and 2016, the country legally exported more than 47,000 kilograms of wild-collected orchids. However, discrepancies exist between Nepal’s export data and those of its trading partners, arising from issues such as mismatched and unreported trade amounts and species being sold under different names.

Recent findings suggest that the trade in animal and plant species is regulated mostly under the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES) agreement, which is designed to protect wildlife from exploitation. Although Nepal joined the convention more than 50 years ago, it did not introduce legislation to implement CITES until 2017.

The orchid Dendrobium longicornu is sought after for its black-haired canes and fragrant white and orange blooms.

The orchid Dendrobium longicornu is sought after for its black-haired canes and fragrant white and orange blooms.

In a recent development, all but two species of orchid in Nepal are now listed in CITES Appendix II, which includes species that are not currently threatened with extinction but could be if their trade is not regulated. The government must create a management blueprint and a formal assessment to confirm that harvesting a species for trade won’t harm the survival of the wild population. “We haven’t prepared such a management plan for any orchid species yet. So, their trade is still considered illegal here,” Bashyal adds. Violation of the CITES Act can lead to a fine of up to 100,000 Nepalese rupees (US$660), one year in prison, or both.

Bashyal started researching orchids in 2018, when conservation fieldwork revealed the extent of harvesting and trade of the plants.

Bashyal started researching orchids in 2018, when conservation fieldwork revealed the extent of harvesting and trade of the plants.

Bashyal demonstrates a survey technique to a member of her team.

Bashyal demonstrates a survey technique to a member of her team.

Bashyal (right) and a team from the non-profit organization Greenhood Nepal have partnered with forest officials and local community members to form an anti-poaching taskforce.

Bashyal (right) and a team from the non-profit organization Greenhood Nepal have partnered with forest officials and local community members to form an anti-poaching taskforce.

Sources indicate that bashyal first became involved in orchid research by chance. In 2018, while working on a conifer tree conservation project for non-profit organization Greenhood Nepal in Kathmandu, she visited several regional sites across the country and was often approached by people asking about the demand for orchids in the city. When her team investigated further, it realized that many people living in the villages were harvesting or actively trading the plants.

Sources indicate that this illegal trading was often overlooked by authorities, according to Bashyal. Before suggesting a way to stop it, the team had to understand the market — specifically which species were being taken, their conservation status and how the supply chain operated. To do this, it visited orchid trading hubs across Nepal and spoke to harvesters, traders and enforcement officials.

The Makawanpur region of Nepal is home to orchids, yew trees and a rich diversity of other wildlife.

The Makawanpur region of Nepal is home to orchids, yew trees and a rich diversity of other wildlife.

“The local people provide information on where orchids are harvested, moved, gathered and how much they sold orchids for,” she says. During these visits, the team shared its research and spoke about the importance of conservation, which was well received, she says. “After all, an unsustainable harvesting of the orchids severely threatens local livelihood and income,” she adds.

Bashyal’s team at Greenhood Nepal learnt that several orchid species, including Satyrium nepalense and Pleione praecox, are harvested in large quantities for their medicinal value. Overharvesting an orchid species that is in decline can easily lead to its extinction in the wild, which makes understanding a species’ population and distribution crucial for creating sustainable harvesting practices.

After the field trips, Bashyal’s team created a series of policy briefs, drafted conservation frameworks and started the anti-poaching taskforce in collaboration with the region’s governmental forest management office to document illegal activity and conduct patrols.

The team is also developing comprehensive identification manuals and guidelines for regulators. Many existing manuals focus on identifying whole plants and flowers, but traded items can include the orchid’s thickened stem and fleshy underground storage organs, called tubers. Some orchids are boiled, or dried for several hours or days before being traded.

In some parts of Nepal, communities can earn a good income from harvesting and selling orchids alongside other medicinal plants. For many, medicinal plants are their sole source of income. “Simply telling the locals ‘you are not supposed to do this’ will not stop them from harvesting,” Bashyal states. For this reason, imposing a blanket ban on trade might not be effective.

Bashyal emphasizes that tracking the wildlife trade is complex and often requires navigating delicate legal territory. Researchers must also have patience when interviewing informants. “Thus, it also comes down to following research ethics, respect and treating local knowledge as a valuable resource to build trust,” Bashyal says. “Only after that, can we have data and develop any intervention.”.

The forests of Makawanpur support an array of native orchids.

The forests of Makawanpur support an array of native orchids.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that hair loss isn’t always dramatic. It can be incremental. You start noticing a bit more scalp in harsh bathroom lighting, a tiny bald spot when you tie your hair up in a ponytail. The shower drain is more clogged than usual. Not long ago, hair-loss treatments meant topical remedies, supplements, or a flight to Turkey. Luckily, red-light therapy brings the potential for hair regrowth into your home—no clinical appointment required.

Beyond skin rejuvenation, clinical studies suggest red-light therapy can help energize hair follicles, increase blood circulation in the scalp, reduce inflammation, and lower dihydrotestosterone levels—a hormone that causes hair loss and thinning. Red-light therapy also supports adenosine triphosphate (ATP) production, which helps provide oxygen and blood flow to the scalp and triggers follicles to remain in the hair growth phase.

To determine the best red-light therapy for hair growth, I tapped five WIRED tech reviewers who've dealt with hair loss themselves. We assessed red-light caps, hands-free helmets with full scalp coverage, and low-level laser therapy (LLLT) or photobiomodulation devices for 16 weeks. Along the way, I reviewed the research, spoke with dermatologists, and tracked ease of use. These are the favorites that produced meaningful results and earned our trust.

Be sure to check out our other wellness and skin-care guides, including the Best LED Masks, Best Hair Dryers, and Best Blow Dry Brushes.

Love WIRED? Add us as a preferred source on Google to see more of us.

Updated November 2026: I added the Capillus HairBand to Honorable Mentions, and I included a product to avoid. Prices, links, and product information were also updated.

It has been revealed that to start, I consulted board-certified dermatologists and referred to clinical trials to help determine what features to look for when shopping for a device. I test these devices with several tech reviewers on our team, all of whom have personal experience with hair thinning or loss to different degrees. Most of these at-home gadgets call for a 16-week treatment cycle. We follow the brands' directions and record any visible results along the way.

According to recent reports, we monitor changes in hair count, hair density, and scalp health, but effectiveness is only one of the factors we consider. We also judge ease of use, functionality, and comfort. We note the specific wavelengths of light and whether the treatment options feel tolerable or difficult to integrate into everyday routines.

Industry observers note that we also prioritize safety, checking for FDA clearance, automatic shut-off features, and overall durability of the design. To date, our testers have not experienced any side effects, but we would have documented them had they.

I'm testing the Foreo Flip Play and the Theradome PRO Laser Hair Growth Helmet LH80.

After 12 weeks, I didn’t notice a difference in hair length—I did get a haircut halfway through testing—but I did spot latest follicles sprouting along my scalp and sideburn area. My hairstylist mentioned that my hair felt thicker, and I noticed less breakage and hair caught in bristles when brushing. My balding roommate also tested the CurrentBody helmet, and he noted that his hair also felt thicker and that there was new growth around the scalp.

The circular earmuffs protect sensitive ears with a cushy, removable faux leather cloth, and they can be adjusted several inches up or down to ensure a comfortable fit. You can also connect the device to Bluetooth and play any type of audio during sessions, because God forbid I be left alone with my thoughts for 10 minutes a day. My only complaint is that the ear covers aren’t the easiest to adjust and would oftentimes pull out my hair when I removed the helmet. Nevertheless, this is the best red-light therapy for fuller hair. See my full review here. —Molly Higgins.

Recent findings suggest that at first glance, the HigherDose Red Light Hat looks like your everyday baseball cap, with a brand logo embroidered across the top—until you notice the little battery cap and controller on the back, or the 120 LED light bulbs lining the inside. While I don’t suffer from natural hair loss, I’ve struggled with trichotillomania since my teens. Part of what initiated the habit is that any time my sensitive scalp gets irritated, the itchiness drives me to pull at the hair around the spot. But in the months I’ve been using the HigherDose hat, I have felt like my scalp has been happier, with fewer irritated spots and overall itchiness, leaving me less likely to reach for my scalp. Last October, after my first month with this device, my hairstylist saw healthier regrowth instead of the breakage she usually sees. In January, she took another look and noted that my usual problem spot on the back of my head had grown in better than ever. She didn’t find any reaction on my scalp, either, from four months of using the device, and my roots look thicker all around my head.

In a recent development, similar to my infrared brushes, I find that my hair is a tad oilier after use; both types of devices employ infrared light that can lock in moisture. It’s not a problem on days when my hair is clean, but if my hair is already dirty, using this hat requires an immediate shower. Overall, though, using the HigherDose hat has had a serious payoff for me, my scalp, and my hair. See my full review here. —Nena Farrell.

I seem to rival a golden retriever in terms of shedding, and my sensitive scalp makes things itchy and flaky. To nip it in the bud, I tested the iRestore Elite device, along with the Max Growth kit. It sits right on the crown of your head, and it does heat up quite a bit as the red light puts focused emphasis on your scalp. The red-light exposure has helped prevent flare-ups, as I have none to note from my time testing it. That’s a feat in itself.

Sources indicate that however, I’m not the success story here. I recruited a balding tester (my husband, who also gets to give products a spin) who wanted to give it a go to see if it would help with his receding hairline. After three months of consistent use, his hair density has bounced back significantly. It’s a regular sight to see him drink his morning coffee while waiting for the Elite’s 12-minute run time to wrap up. The accompanying Max Growth hair products smell wonderful, and they also played a contributing role in his follicular blossoming. Now, if only he would stop taking them out of my shower. Unlike other devices on this list, GroWell is designed to be used every other day rather than every day to give your scalp a rest day to process the cellular stimulation (photobiomodulation). Also, unlike others, its wattage is limited to avoid oversaturating follicles past what studies show is the optimal 3 to 4 joules. What GroWell does do is treat your scalp with a proprietary combination of lasers and LEDs to create a blanket of energy you can feel lightly warming your scalp. (GrowWell's therapy-grade laser and LED diodes are proprietary to Apira, the tech giant behind iGrow and GroWell, and are not the same as the generic diodes common in lower-end caps sold online.) Sources indicate that I've been using the laser cap for two months and have grown my always-thin and fine hair out for the first time in 15 years. It's worked well enough that I'm not asked as many questions about it as you might expect—everyone assumes I just shaved my head purely by choice now that they see me with a pretty regular amount of hair for a middle-aged guy. Hairmax LaserBand 82 ComfortFlex for $849: Unlike the usual helmet- or hat-based regrowth devices, the Hairmax LaserBand is a 3-inch-thick, flexible headband studded with 82 concentrated lasers rather than LEDs. Hooga Red Light Therapy Hat for Hair Growth for $299: I was excited to try this more affordable red-light hat after loving my experience with the HigherDose one, but I found myself unimpressed and actually uncomfortable while using it. The Hooga Red Light Therapy Hat looks like a baseball cap, but it doesn’t have a battery, so you have to stay plugged into the wall the entire time you use it. Feels a little pointless to look outdoor-ready when you can’t actually use it on the go. It also got too hot for me to wear comfortably. —Nena Farrell.

Does Red-Light Therapy Work for Hair Loss?

Yes—research suggests low-level light therapy can work for certain types of hair loss, such as androgenetic alopecia, also known as male or female pattern hair loss. It can help increase hair count, thickness, and density by stimulating hair follicles and boosting cellular activity in the scalp.

In a recent development, that remarked, results depend heavily on the type and severity of hair loss. Red-light therapy works best in cases of mild to moderate thinning and may be less effective for advanced hair loss or scarring conditions like cicatricial alopecia. Consistency also matters. You typically need regular, ongoing use to maintain results, and benefits can diminish if treatments stop.

What Wavelength of Red Light Is Best for Hair Restoration?

According to the American Hair Loss Association, wavelengths in the range of 630 to 680 nanometers are ideal for hair regrowth. These wavelengths are known to support increased blood flow to the scalp, boost cellular activity, and help reduce inflammation. Some clinical studies specifically cite 650 nanometers as an especially effective wavelength.

Sources indicate that red-light devices that use medical-grade laser diodes tend to deliver more targeted and consistent light than standard LEDs, but both can stimulate hair follicles at the right wavelengths. For best results, look for FDA-cleared devices that list their wavelengths and power output.

How to Use Red-Light Therapy for Hair Growth.

Consistency is the most crucial part of any red-light therapy routine. Most devices require at least three months of use before noticeable results are observed, and some may take longer. Follow the manufacturer’s instructions, as treatment schedules vary by device, but most recommend sessions three to five times per week. The hair growth is preserved only with continued use, so you’ll need ongoing maintenance sessions.

Industry observers note that always start with a clean and dry scalp so the light can reach your hair follicles without interference from oils or styling products. Some devices include protective eyewear, and if yours does, wear it during treatment. Make sure to wipe the device down with a gentle disinfectant before or after each session to prevent buildup on the LEDs.

Topical regrowth treatments can complement red-light therapy and may help support thicker hair. A few randomized clinical trials suggest that combining minoxidil (2 percent or 5 percent) with red-light therapy can improve hair density and encourage faster regrowth compared to using either treatment alone. For a natural alternative, some research has found rosemary oil to produce results comparable to 2 percent minoxidil for androgenetic alopecia, though the evidence isn’t as extensive as it is for minoxidil.

If you’re pregnant or have an underlying medical condition, talk to your healthcare provider before starting any form of red-light therapy.

Is Red-Light Therapy for Hair Growth Safe?

Yes—for most people, red-light therapy is considered a safe and noninvasive treatment with minimal side effects when used as intended. Still, it's always worth consulting a health care professional before starting any sort of treatment. This is especially the case for anyone with photosensitive conditions or autoimmune disorders that affect light sensitivity.

I prefer devices that are FDA-cleared because it means they've met certain safety standards for consumer use. But keep in mind that the clearance process is less rigorous than the FDA approval pathway, as it just requires manufacturers to prove their product is “substantially equivalent” to an already legally marketed device. Also, FDA clearance isn't a guarantee of results; it simply means it's considered safe to use as directed at home.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Boris Rosenfeld reveals DW a photo of him with his daughter Sofia and can't hold back tears.
  • Recent findings suggest that helives in Israel, while Sofia is in Russia.
  • On October 7, a court in Moscow sentenced Rosenfeld to three and a half years in a penal colony.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Boris Rosenfeld reveals DW a photo of him with his daughter Sofia and can't hold back tears. "This was the last time we saw her. Then she left for Moscow, and this whole case began," he says.

Recent findings suggest that helives in Israel, while Sofia is in Russia. For more than a month now, she has been behind bars on charges of financing extremism. The case goes back to two donations totaling 2,000 rubles (about $30) to the late opposition politician Alexei Navalny'sAnti-Corruption Foundation (FBK), which the Russian authorities have since designated as extremist.

On October 7, a court in Moscow sentenced Rosenfeld to three and a half years in a penal colony.

Rosenfeld is a prominent ornithologist who has devoted her life to studying and protecting Arcticbirds. "Sofia was an avid young naturalist from childhood. She loved birds, horses and dogs," her father stated as he leafed through a photo album.

Sofia was a teenager when the family moved to Israel but she returned to Russia a few years later and now holds both Russian and Israeli citizenship.

She studied biology at Moscow State University and developed a significant scientific career in Russia. Her colleague, Alexandra Panyutina, who now also lives in Israel, explained that Rosenfeld was devoted to her work from an early age.

"Birds and the Arctic are the defining passions of her life," she mentioned.

Rosenfeld was among the first Russian researchers to develop a systematic approach to monitoring migratory bird populations. To support her research, she even developed a special aircraft.

Sources indicate that "They could fly at almost the same speed as the birds and observe them from a low altitude," notes Dmitry (name changed), a colleague of Rosenfeld's. "It quickly became clear that this was a unique method.".

Sources indicate that rosenfeld is considered to be one of the leading figures in Russian ornithology. Her work has extended well beyond Russia and she has been deeply involved in international research projects. In the field of migratory bird conservation, cross-border cooperation is essential.

Helmut Kruckenberg, the head of the German Institute for Wetlands and Waterbird Research (IWWR), said Rosenfeld was highly respected within the international scientific community.

"She has done an enormous amount for nature conservation and for the protection of Siberian and Arctic species," he remarked. "What is happening to her is simply beyond comprehension for us.".

In the summer of 2021, when Russian authorities designated Alexei Navalny's Anti-Corruption Foundation, also known as FBK, as an extremist organization, Rosenfeld was on a remote Arctic expedition without a phone or access to the internet. Therefore, she did not cancel her regular donations to the FBK immediately, doing so only after her return to the Russian capital Moscow.

Sources indicate that her friend Olga (name changed) described Sofia as a person of absolute honesty. According to her, Rosenfeld's donations to Navalny's foundation reflected a genuine desire to fight corruption. Through her work in Russia's regions, she had seen plenty of it firsthand.

"She was never involved in political activism. Her donations were solely intended to support anti-corruption work," said her father Boris Rosenfeld. "It's unthinkable".

It has been revealed that for him and others close to her, the sentence came as a shock. Although prosecutors had requested a five-year prison term, friends and colleagues expected that she would receive a fine at most.

There were reasons for that expectation. According to calculations by independent media outlet Mediazona, about 85% of convictions in the 225 cases involving donations to Navalny's foundation have so far resulted in non-custodial sentences. Yet Rosenfeld got three and a half years in a penal colony.

It has been revealed that just a few months after Rosenfeld defended her doctoral dissertation in October 2025, her home was searched. She was also subject to travel restrictions. She continued to work but she had to cancel her annual summer expedition to the Arctic.

Sources indicate that even on the day of the sentencing, her conversations with  her colleagues focused largely on science:  "We discussed how the work could continue in Sofia's absence," Olga said. "But no one really believed she would end up in prison.".

"The only thing we think about now is how to bring her here," Boris Rosenfeld says as he looks at the pictures from Sofia's last visit.

In a recent development, friends and colleagues who spoke to DW say that his daughter never considered leaving Russia, even as the prospect of a prison sentence loomed. "Sofia would never have left. She simply can't imagine life without geese," states Dmitry.

According to recent reports, now, her family, friends and colleagues are campaigning to have her sentence overturned. More than 1,000 people have signed an appeal to Russia's Presidential Council for Human Rights.

Boris Rosenfeld is also hoping for support from Israel but so far Israeli consular officials have not been granted access to his daughter in detention.

It has been revealed that the two continue to write to each other and he is trying to keep his spirits high: "She writes that she's trying to adjust to life in prison, and that it's hard," he says. "But she's a strong person.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ever had something to say, but later? WhatsApp now lets you schedule messages that will be automatically sent at a designated time.

In a recent development, you can line up messages to be delivered anytime from 10 minutes to 14 days later, either to your one-on-one or group chats. Scheduled messages can have text, photos, and videos.

The feature has been one of the most requested features on WhatsApp, the manufacturer remarked in a blog post.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

Sources indicate that to schedule a message in WhatsApp, press and hold the send button, then pick the time and date for the message to arrive. Vital: The receiving party won't know that it's a scheduled message, and they'll be delighted that you remembered their birthday even though you merely used an AI agent to schedule everyone's birthday messages automatically (we kid, we would never).

Just like normal messages, the scheduled messages will be end-to-end encrypted. Also, WhatsApp points out that they'll be sent even if your phone is off or out of battery.

According to WhatsApp, scheduled messages are rolling out globally "over the coming weeks.".

#128107. Erdogan's political fate may be determined by Turkey's Kurds

Erdogan's political fate may be determined by Turkey's Kurds

📅 03 Apr 2023 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1512 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNN

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Turkey’s persecuted pro-Kurdish party has emerged as a kingmaker in the country’s upcoming election, playing a decisive role that may just tip the balance enough to unseat two-decade ruler Recep Tayyip Erdogan.
  • In a key setback to the Turkish president and leader of the Justice and Development Party (AK Party), the pro-Kurdish Peoples’ Democratic Party (HDP) last month announced that it would not put forward its own presidential candidate, a move analysts say allows its supporters to vote for Erdogan’s main rival.
  • Recent findings suggest that “We are facing a turning point that will shape the future of Turkey and (its) society,” noted the HDP in a statement on March 23.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Turkey’s persecuted pro-Kurdish party has emerged as a kingmaker in the country’s upcoming election, playing a decisive role that may just tip the balance enough to unseat two-decade ruler Recep Tayyip Erdogan.

In a key setback to the Turkish president and leader of the Justice and Development Party (AK Party), the pro-Kurdish Peoples’ Democratic Party (HDP) last month announced that it would not put forward its own presidential candidate, a move analysts say allows its supporters to vote for Erdogan’s main rival.

Recent findings suggest that “We are facing a turning point that will shape the future of Turkey and (its) society,” noted the HDP in a statement on March 23. “To fulfill our historical responsibility against the one-man rule, we will not field a presidential candidate in (the) May 14 elections.”.

It is a twist of irony for the Turkish strongman, who spent the better half of the past decade cracking down on the party after it began chipping away at his voter base. Its former leader Selahattin Demirtas has been in prison for nearly seven years and the party faces possible closure by a court for suspected collusion with the militant Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK) and affiliated groups. But its influence may nonetheless determine the course of Turkey’s politics.

The HDP’s decision not to field a candidate came just three days after head of the Republican People’s Party (CHP) Kemal Kilicdaroglu, Erdogan’s main rival, visited the party’s co-chairs. He told reporters that the solution to Turkey’s problems, “including the Kurdish problem” lies in parliament,” according to Turkish media.

Industry observers note that kilicdaroglu, who represents the six-party Nation Alliance opposition bloc, is the strongest contender to run against Erdogan in years. And while the HDP hasn’t yet unveiled whether it will put its weight behind him, analysts say it is the kingmaker in the elections.

Erdogan's 'polar opposite' wants to replace him as president of Turkey.

Recent findings suggest that “It was a carefully crafted political discourse,” Hisyar Ozsoy, deputy co-chair of the HDP and a member of parliament from the predominantly Kurdish province of Diyarbakir, told CNN. “We are not going to have our own candidate, and we will leave it to the international community to interpret it the way they wish.”.

Experts say the crackdown on the HDP is rooted in the threat it poses to Erdogan politically, as well as its position as one of the main parties representing Turkey’s Kurds, an ethnic minority from which a separatist militant movement has emerged.

Industry observers note that the party and the Kurdish people have had a complicated relationship with Erdogan. The leader courted the Kurds in earlier years by granting them more rights and reversing restrictions on the use of their language. Relations with the HDP were also cordial once, as Erdogan worked with the party on a brief peace process with the PKK.

But ties between Erdogan and the HDP later turned sour, and the HDP fell under a sweeping crackdown aimed at the PKK and their affiliates.

Kurds are the biggest minority in Turkey, making up between 15% and 20% of the population, according to Minority Rights Group International.

It is unclear if the HDP will endorse Kilicdaroglu, but analysts say that the deliberate distance may be beneficial for the opposition candidate.

It has been revealed that the accusations against the HDP place it in a precarious position during the elections. It currently faces a case in Turkey’s Constitutional Court over suspected ties to the PKK, which is designated as a terrorist group by Turkey, the United States and the European Union. Knowing it may be banned at any moment, its candidates are running under the Green Left Party in parliament.

If the opposition is seen as allying with the HDP, Erdogan’s AK Party may use its influence in the media to discredit it as being pro-PKK, remarked Murat Somer, a political science professor at Koc University in Istanbul and author of Return to Point Zero, a book on the Turkish-Kurdish question in Turkey.

Recent findings suggest that the HDP’s threat to Erdogan’s hold on power became apparent after the June 2015 election, the first general election it participated in. It won 13% of the seats, denying the ruling AK Party its majority for the first time since 2002. Erdogan, however, called a snap election five months later, which led to a drop in the HDP’s support to 10.7%, as well as the restoration of the AK Party’s overall majority.

Sources indicate that “They are a kingmaker in these elections because the HDP gets about half of the votes of the Kurdish population in Turkey,” noted Somer, adding that the other, more conservative Kurdish voters have traditionally voted for Erdogan’s AK Party. And last month, the Free Cause Party (HUDA-PAR), a tiny Kurdish-Islamist party announced support for Erdogan in the elections. The party has never won seats in parliament.

Erdogan's political fate may rest on his response to the earthquake.

The HDP knows that its position is key to the outcome of next month’s vote, but that it’s also in a delicate situation.

“We want to play the game wisely, and we need to be very careful,” mentioned Ozsoy, adding that the party wants to avoid a “contaminated political climate” where the elections are polarized “between a very ugly ultra-nationalist discourse against Kilicdaroglu and others.”.

The party was founded in 2012 with a number of aims, mentioned Ozsoy, one of which was “peaceful and democratic resolution of the Kurdish conflict.”.

Somer mentioned that the party was seen to be “an initiative” of the PKK, which later led to a heavy government crackdown on it in the name of counterterrorism.

Its former leader Demirtas remains an influential figure.

The Turkish government has been trying to link the HDP to the PKK but has so far failed to prove “a real connection,” said Asli Aydintasbas, a visiting fellow at the Brookings Institution in Washington, DC.

A post-Erdogan Turkey may give some breathing space to the Kurds and Kurdish-dominated parties in Turkey, Aydintasbas told CNN, noting that many Kurdish voters have recently left Erdogan’s camp. “For HDP, this is more than just an ideological choice,” she mentioned. “It’s a matter of survival.”.

Ozsoy notes his party understands what’s at stake, not only for Turkey’s Kurds but for all its minorities.

“We are aware of our responsibility here. We are aware of our role. We know we are in a kingmaker position,” the HDP lawmaker stated.

Two women arrested for not wearing hijab following ‘yogurt attack’.

Two women were arrested in Iran for failing to wear the hijab in public, after a man threw a tub of yogurt at them at a store in the city of Shandiz on Thursday, according to Mizan News Agency, the state-run outlet for Iran’s judiciary.

Oil prices surge after OPEC+ producers announce surprise cuts.

Industry observers note that oil prices spiked Monday after OPEC+ producers unexpectedly revealed that they would cut output. Brent crude, the global benchmark, jumped 5.31% to $84.13 a barrel, while WTI, the US benchmark, rose 5.48% to $79.83. Both were the sharpest price rises in almost a year. The collective output cut by the nine members of OPEC+ totals 1.66 million barrels per day.

Iran blames Israel for the killing of second IRGC officer, vows to respond.

Industry observers note that A second Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) officer died following an attack in Syria on Friday, according to Iranian state media on Sunday. Iranian state media remarked the Iranian military adviser died after an Israeli attack near the Syrian capital Damascus left him wounded. The attack also killed another IRGC officer. In a tweet on Sunday, Iranian government spokesman Ali Bahadori Jahromi said the alleged Israeli attack wouldn’t go unanswered. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Nasser Kanaani said on Sunday that Iran has the right to respond to “state terrorism.”.

Iranian-American comedian Maz Jobrani, who has been touring the Middle East, spoke to CNN’s Becky Anderson about his support for the protests in his homeland, saying that he used his standup comedy platform to highlight the “brutality against the Iranian people.”.

“It was an opportunity for me to say, ‘let’s keep fighting,’” he mentioned.

An Iranian state news outlet is gloating at what it sees as the demise of the US dollar.

IRNA recreated a popular meme to mark China and Brazil’s decision to reportedly ditch the US dollar as an intermediary in trade, citing the Chinese state news outlet, China Daily. It demonstrates two men representing China and Brazil posing in front of a grave labelled “USD.”.

Recent findings suggest that the meme was pinned to the top of IRNA’s Twitter page, and was met with laughter and ridicule. “Dream on,” stated another user, pointing to the dollar’s use as the main reserve currency around the world.

China Daily said that the agreement was part of “the rising global use of the Chinese renminbi.” It would reportedly enable China and Brazil to conduct trade and financial transactions using local currencies instead of the dollar.

The Portuguese second-tier team hosting Celtic in Europe

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Portuguese second-tier side Torreense have not played top-flight football since the 1991-92 campaign, but are making their debut in the Europa League this season.
  • S.C.U Torreense's league fixtures this season include meetings with the 'B' teams of Sporting, Benfica and Porto.
  • But the Portuguese second division club, located 35 miles north of Lisbon, are in this season's Europa League after stunning giants Sporting to win the Taca de Portugal in May.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Portuguese second-tier side Torreense have not played top-flight football since the 1991-92 campaign, but are making their debut in the Europa League this season.

S.C.U Torreense's league fixtures this season include meetings with the 'B' teams of Sporting, Benfica and Porto.

But the Portuguese second division club, located 35 miles north of Lisbon, are in this season's Europa League after stunning giants Sporting to win the Taca de Portugal in May.

"This is a landmark moment," Andre Sabino, the club's director of football and CEO told BBC Sport.

Torreense had never played a European home match before their 2-1 defeat by Sunderland in October and welcome Celtic to Leiria on Thursday (20:00 GMT).

They won at Norwegian side Lillestrom on their debut but lost heavily in Hungary against Ferencvaros before beating Ararat-Armenia last time out.

Managed by Luis Tralhao, whose brother Joao is an assistant to Jose Mourinho at Real Madrid, the club are hoping to do more than just make up the numbers.

"It is something extraordinary for Torreense. These are clubs with huge histories, strong identities and enormous European experience," Sabino added.

"To be able to share the same competition and compete against them is a privilege. But we don't want to simply participate. We want to compete.".

Torreense captain and Cape Verde international Stopira (pictured above) scored a penalty in extra time as his side beat Sporting 2-1 in the Taca de Portugal final earlier this year.

Sources indicate that second-tier Beira-Mar played in the 1999-2000 Uefa Cup, although they were a top-flight team at the time of qualifying. But Torreense are the first team from the second division to qualify by winning the Taca de Portugal.

"The Portuguese Cup has been played since 1938 in its current model and it was the first time that a second division team won it," Portuguese football journalist and ex-Benfica goalkeeper Jose Delgado told BBC Sport.

"You can imagine when they could defeat a giant club like Sporting in the final, it was quite a surprise and for the city, it's something very, very special.".

After beating Lillestrom, they have already exceeded the expectations of some. "I thought that Torreense could go through the Europa League with no points," added Delgado.

With Portugal ranked outside Uefa's top five leagues, every club in the Champions League, Europa League or Conference League has a responsibility to perform well to earn their nation important ranking points.

"For Portuguese football, everybody [thought it] was nice that a club like Torreense won the cup but also we had some concerns," said Delgado.

Recent findings suggest that "The first game everybody thought that Torreense had no chance against Lillestrom and they won. It was quite a good surprise. But it's like a fairytale for Torreense because they are a small club.".

Torreense's Estadio Manuel Marques has a capacity smaller than 45 of the 48 clubs in England's sixth tier.

As their 2,431-capacity home at Estadio Manuel Marques does not pass Uefa's stadium criteria, they will instead face Celtic almost 47 miles away at the Municipal Stadium in Leiria.

In a recent development, "Obviously, it is not ideal," Sabino explained. "Playing at home should mean playing in your own stadium, in front of your own supporters and in the environment that represents your club.

"But at the same time, we understand the logistical and regulatory requirements involved in European competition.

"We have to look at the bigger picture. We are extremely grateful for the opportunity to compete in the Europa League and we will make Leiria feel as much like home as possible.".

The additional travel has not deterred supporters from watching their beloved club face significant European names.

"Our supporters and our people are what make a home, regardless of the kilometres. The response from our supporters has been fantastic," Sabino added.

"They understand that this is a historic moment for Torreense and they want to experience it with us.

"We hope to see Leiria filled with Torreense colours and feel that support from the first minute.".

Torreense pocketed 630,000 euros (Â£533,000) for their win over Lillestrom.

It has been revealed that torreense missed out on a return to Portugal's top division for the first time since 1991-92 after a 2-0 two-legged defeat by Casa Pia in a promotion/relegation play-off in May. And fell at the first hurdle in their defence of the Taca de Portugal.

But qualification for the Europa League's league phase guarantees a financial injection of at least 5m euros (Â£4.2m).

Every positive result and extra round reached adds more to that pot.

In a recent development, "For a club like Torreense, it is a very significant amount," Sabino explained. "It gives us an opportunity to strengthen the club in several areas and to accelerate projects that otherwise would naturally take much longer.

Recent findings suggest that "However, we have to be very responsible. Success can create opportunities but it also creates responsibilities.

It has been revealed that "Our objective is not simply to spend more because we have more resources. We want to invest intelligently, strengthen the structure of the club and create conditions for sustainable growth.".

Torreense played competitively against Sporting's main and 'B' teams last season, something they will also do this year against Porto.

Torreense have made 19 new signings from across the globe for this season.

In a recent development, as well as turning to Portugal's top flight for five newly introduced recruits, other signings have come from France, Greece, Spain, Serbia, Portugal, Brazil, Denmark, Morocco and Germany. The majority from outside those countries' top leagues.

Of their 32-man senior squad, just four are Portuguese.

It has been revealed that "It has been a very different challenge," Sabino explained. "European football changes the perception of the club and naturally makes Torreense more attractive to certain players, but it also increases expectations.".

Industry observers note that last season, Torreense missed out on automatic promotion on goal difference before losing the play-off. This term they have won only two of their opening 10 league games and sit 13th.

With the overwhelming majority of football fans in Portugal supporting one of the 'big three' of Porto, Benfica and Sporting - Delgado notes sometimes home fans even cheer for their more illustrious opponents when they visit.

"Right now I think that there is a great sympathy about Torreense, but I don't think they will get many more [fans] because of this presence," he added.

"Maybe this presence will make some investors look at them in a different way and put some money in the club.".

Time to rise? Ranking European football's sleeping giants.

Spain Under-21 striker admits the pace of the Premier League has surprised him but states he must stay calm over goal drought at Fulham.

According to recent reports, the first thing Rita Hayworth’s great nephew says when he walks in is: “Sorry I’m late.” Gonzalo García is not late, but it’s very like him: he is impeccably polite, accommodating, and there’s an almost gentle quality to him, a calm that’s not common but can help, especially in moments when the pressure builds. There’s a reason one of the coaches standing in the rain by the pitch where Spain’s under‑21s have just finished training says everyone here loves García. The Fulham striker shakes hands, introduces himself and ducks into the dressing room to change; then a few minutes later he’s back, apologising for a wait that wasn’t one.

Time to talk, so let’s start with Tinseltown, the family tale. García laughs. His great-aunt, born Margarita Carmen Cansino, was among the biggest stars in Hollywood, although he’s not sure he’s seen any of her films. His grandfather was a surgeon and others in the family followed. His uncles played rugby for Spain, but that wasn’t his thing. As for him, he enrolled in a degree in business management and analytics, and reckons he might have liked law, yet even that wasn’t his chosen field.

Germany's religious freedom report: Authoritarian regimes, holy wars, and spies abroad

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1191 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the report spans more than 150 pages, but its conclusion can be summed up in a single sentence: "The global situation regarding freedom of religion and belief deteriorated during the reporting period," said Thomas Rachel, the German government's commissioner for freedom of religion and belief, and a member of parliament for the center-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU).
  • The government has issued a dedicated report on freedom of religion and belief around the world.
  • To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the report spans more than 150 pages, but its conclusion can be summed up in a single sentence: "The global situation regarding freedom of religion and belief deteriorated during the reporting period," said Thomas Rachel, the German government's commissioner for freedom of religion and belief, and a member of parliament for the center-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU). Recently adopted by the Cabinet, the government's fourth report on the subject covers developments from 2023 to 2025.

The government has issued a dedicated report on freedom of religion and belief around the world. According to the report, this freedom is facing "increasing pressure" globally. The focus is not primarily on the suppression of religious institutions or structures, but on the situation of individuals who hold a religious belief, or none at all.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Industry observers note that the importance of religious freedom is reflected in the way the government commissioner describes the concern: "Religion and faith are of great importance to four out of five people around the world and are central to their identity. People wake up with God and go to sleep with God. It is part of their everyday lives." Research by the Pew Research Center suggests that about 84% of the world's population identifies with a certain religion.

Sources indicate that at a time when authoritarian regimes are gaining ground and expanding their surveillance capabilities, the report paints a bleak picture. The growing number of violent conflicts, the rise of authoritarian rule, and the spread of populism have led to "painful restrictions on freedom of religion and belief around the world.".

The German government report does not attempt to provide a statistical tally of attacks or the number of people facing persecution. Instead, it examines 30 countries as case studies where, in the federal government's view, freedom of religion and belief is being restricted. These include about six countries each from Africa, Asia, and the Arab world. In Europe, the report focuses on Belarus, Russia, Ukraine, and Turkey, while in Latin America it highlights Mexico, Nicaragua, and Cuba. It also identifies shortcomings in five of the world's six most populous countries: China, India, Indonesia, Pakistan, and Nigeria.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In a recent development, regarding India, the report refers to "Hindu nationalist efforts" that threaten the equal treatment of all officially recognized religions. It states that the generally peaceful coexistence of different faiths is "repeatedly overshadowed by tensions and, at times, violence." Both Muslim and Christian communities report growing intolerance and hate speech. According to the report, violent Hindu extremist groups have carried out a "large number of physical attacks" against Muslims, while the police and government authorities often respond inadequately.

In China, the German government identifies a "significant tightening of the legal framework of state control at the expense of freedom of religion and belief." According to the report, this particularly affects Uyghurs, Tibetans and churches that lack official state approval and are subject to harsh measures by the authorities. The law on the "Promotion of Ethnic Unity and Progress," which came into force on July 1, 2026, subordinates religion to "the formation of national identity" and patriotic education.

According to recent reports, one of the countries where the situation has deteriorated most dramatically is Nicaragua, which has severely restricted freedom of religion and belief since 2018. The repression has primarily targeted the Catholic Church. According to the report, "intimidation, persecution, imprisonment, and expulsion" have forced around 130 priests and nuns to leave the country.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The reports reserves some of its sharpest criticism for Kirill, the patriarch of the Russian Orthodox Church. Under his leadership, the church has strongly supported Russia's war against Ukraine and portrayed it as a "holy war." According to the report, "weapons are blessed, Russian soldiers are absolved of their sins, and donations are collected for the war." It is perhaps the clearest example in the report of how religion can be used to justify oppression and violence.

In a recent development, the report explicitly addresses the threat posed by "transnational repression" (TNR), which it describes as a "growing global problem" that also affects Germany. The term refers to the persecution or intimidation of individuals by their country of origin beyond its own borders.

Ultimately, it argues, this amounts to a "continuation of domestic repression." Such "cross-border repression" has become considerably easier through the growing availability of digital means of repression, including smear campaigns on social media and spyware.

According to recent reports, these forms of pressure range from physical attacks on individuals to digital assaults such as online intimidation and defamation. In some cases, repression is also carried out by threatening family members who remain in the country of origin. Russia and Iran, for example, are identified as the "main perpetrators of transnational repression" in Germany.

China is a particularly prominent example of religious and ideological tensions. Repression by Beijing in Germany primarily targets members of groups that the country's Communist Party classifies as "hostile to the system." These include Uyghurs, Tibetans, and members of the Falun Gong movement. According to the report, they are "also subject to surveillance and repressive measures in Germany," while relatives living in China are pressured.

Thomas Rachel hopes the newly published report will be "discussed in as many Bundestag committees as possible" and that members of parliament will "engage with the concern accordingly." Previous government reports on the subject have been debated in the Bundestag plenary at least once and, in some cases, twice.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In a recent development, the problem's place within the German government has also changed during the current legislative term. Commissioner Thomas Rachel is now based at the Foreign Ministry, while both of his predecessors since 2018 were attached to the Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development. Today, Rachel claims, the importance of religion is being "taken into account" in German foreign policy. He also points to his involvement in the Foreign Ministry's diplomatic training programs.

In a recent development, in doing so, the government led by Chancellor Friedrich Merz (CDU) reversed a structural decision made by the previous center-left coalition, which was led from 2021 to 2025 by Chancellor Olaf Scholz of the Social Democratic Party (SPD). The Scholz government had reduced the issue's prominence by assigning it to the "Religion and Foreign Policy" division. Religion and foreign policy have now regained a more prominent place within government.

Industry observers note that one example is the current foreign minister, Johann Wadephul, who has already visited the Vatican more often than his two predecessors combined. In addition, alongside Rachel, the ministry has for some time maintained a dedicated unit headed by an ambassador that deals with, among other things, "fundamental complications relating to religion and foreign policy.".

It takes two to tango, but Jojo Siwa is looking toward bigger dance numbers.

Over a year and a half after the Dance Moms alum found love with Love Island UK’s Chris Hughes, she revealed she’s ready to become a dance mom of her own.

Industry observers note that as revealed during the Nov. 25 episode of the Petticoat Revolution podcast, her ideal next chapter would be to “have a baby. Be a mom. That’s my next thing.”.

And the 23-year-old is more than ready to hit pause on her professional career in the meantime.

Recent findings suggest that “Obviously that's not a career thing, but like a life thing,” she explained. “Like career, career is doing her thing. She’s always there. She's been there for 15 years. She'll keep going, she'll keep being there.”.

But this is not the first time Siwa has envisioned a long future with Hughes, who she met while filming Celebrity Substantial Brother in the UK in the spring of 2025.

n fact, Siwa previously revealed she puts her daydreams into practice when it comes to Hughes one day getting down on one knee.

“He got me this ring for Christmas last year,” Siwa told E! News of the jewelry she wore on her right hand in an interview alongside her boyfriend in October. "I wear this every day, I’ve never taken it off—sometimes I'll switch it to my other hand just see what it feels like.”.

And while the 33-year-old admitted that Siwa’s trial run with an engagement ring was news to him, the revelation brought a smile to his face.

Industry observers note that “I didn't know she did that, but now I do,” he stated. “It's kind of cute.”.

But sometimes, Siwa revealed, she shimmies a bit too close to the engagement sun for someone who lives so squarely in the public eye.

Industry observers note that “I'll forget that I've done it,” she stated of wearing her ring on that finger. “And I'm like, ‘Oh crap, it's been there too long. Someone's going to get a photo or something.’”.

Though the couple both confirmed there aren’t any immediate intends for wedding bells to be ringing, Hughes affirmed, “One day, of course.”.

As Siwa put it, “We're in a very happy phase of life right now.”.

For a deeper look at Siwa and Hughes' romance, keep reading...

The couple's whirlwind romance unfolded for the whole world to see during their appearance on Celebrity Big Brother.

Recent findings suggest that A year later, Siwa—who split from ex Kath Ebbs following her time on the U.K. the series—released the song "Serendipity" in honor of the now-couple's chance encounter.

Industry observers note that "The only word to explain what happened on this day a year ago… Serendipity," Siwa wrote in an Instagram post. "Today, I’m reminded of the moment that quietly changed everything.".

Less than a month after they put their bond on display in the Big Brother house and emphasizing they were just friends, Hughes and Siwa confirmed they were dating in late May 2025.

At the time, Siwa cheekily nodded at the romance during a cover of "Bette Davis Eyes" at one of her indicates, in which she instead sang "Chris Hughes' eyes.".

The Love Island alum joined Siwa at several stops of her Infinity Heart Tour, which spanned across Europe, the U.K. and the United States. In a sweet glimpse at their backstage moments, Siwa added of the tour in an Instagram post, "The show represents who I want to be as a person and the artist that I wanna be in this lifetime, and it’s translated so well to the crowd.".

Siwa and Hughes stepped out for their first red carpet as a couple at the Dancers Against Cancer's 2025 Gala of the Stars in Beverly Hills, California.

Siwa shared a glimpse into the couple's favorite bonding activity: golfing in a sweet Instagram photo dump of her summertime adventures.

September 2026: A Trip Across the Pond.

In September 2026, Hughes gave his followers a slice of life moment by filming Siwa arriving to his place in England—and naturally they shared a sweet embrace to boot.

October 2026: Coming Back Like a Boomerang.

Siwa and Hughes turned the Gala of the Stars into a date night two years in a row by attending again in 2026.

November 2026: Time for a Family?

Siwa proved her love for Hughes knows no bounds by teasing her next substantial step in life was to become a mom.

"That’s my next thing," Siwa teased during a Nov. 2026 appearance on the Petticoat Revolution podcast. "Career is doing her thing. She’s always there. She's been there for 15 years. She'll keep going, she'll keep being there.”.

#128097. Breaking: The 6 Best Latte Machines for Automatic Espresso Drinks (2026)

📅 23 Aug 2018 • ⏱️ 21m • 📚 Deep Dive (4207 w)
